Content

Census

  • A Census is the official enumeration of the population conducted periodically by the government.
  • Frequency: In India, it is carried out once in every 10 years.
  • Conducting authority: Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MoHA).
  • Legal framework: Census Act, 1948 governs census operations.

History of Census in India

  • First city where Census was conducted: Dacca (Now Dhaka, Bangladesh) in 1830 by Henry Walter (he is also known as "Father of Indian Census").
  • First Census (Non-Synchronized/Incomplete) conducted in 1872 (During Lord Mayo's tenure (1869-1872)).
  • First (Synchronized/Complete) Census conducted in 1881 by the then Census Commissioner of India → W. C. Plowden (During Lord Ripon's tenure (1880-1884)).
  • First Post-Independence Census: 1951.
  • Latest Census conducted: 2011 (15th Census from 1872 and 7th Post-Independence Census).
  • Census 2021: Census 2021 was not conducted due to COVID-19 and has been delayed till October 2024.

Census 2011

  • Registrar General of Census 2011: C. M. Chandramouli (At present: M K Narayan) as of April 2025.
  • Motto: "Our Census, Our Future".
  • Data was collected from: 35 States/UTs and 640 Districts.
  • Census was conducted in two phases:
  • House Listing (April-September 2010).
  • Date of Enumeration: 9-28th February 2011, during population enumeration total 29 questions were asked during.

India's Population in 2011 Census

  • Total population: 1.21 Billion (1210.2 M).
  • India's share in world population: 17.5%.
  • China's share in world population: 19.4%.
  • Male population: 623.7 M (51.54%).
  • Female population: 586.46 M (48.46%).

Concept of Standard Urban Area (SUA) was introduced during: 1971 Census.

  • Maharashtra has the highest slum population.
  • Delhi has the highest slum population among UT.

According to area wise:

  • Highest: Andaman & Nicobar.
  • Lowest: Lakshadweep.

Growth Rate

  • Average annual growth rate (2001-2011): 1.64%.
  • Decadal growth rate (2001-2011): 17.64% (Total increase: 181 M (18.19 Cr) people) → Male: 17.19% and Female: 18.12%.
  • As per 1901 Census: 238 M.
  • According to 1951 Census: 361 M.
  • Highest decadal growth rate (1961-1971): 24.8%.
  • Lowest decadal growth rate (1911-1921): -0.31% (Reason: Due to famine).

Year of the Great Divide (1921) — Reason:

  • Before 1921: High death rate, unstable population.
  • After 1921: Declining death rate, rising population.

Literacy Rate

  • In India, only people aged 7 and above are considered for calculating literacy rates.
  • A person is considered literate if they can read and write with understanding in any language.

Adult (above 15 yrs) literacy: 69.3%.

Overall Literacy Rate

  • As per 2001 Census: 64.83% → Male: 75.85% and Female: 54.16%.
  • As per 2011 Census: 74.04% → Male: 82.14% and Female: 65.46%.
  • As per provisional Census 2011, the literacy rate is 72.98% → Male: 80.9% and Female: 64.63%.
  • Difference in male and female literacy rate: 16.68%.
  • State with highest difference in male and female literacy rate: Rajasthan (27.85%). 2nd: Jharkhand.
  • State with least difference in male and female literacy rate: Meghalaya and 2nd: Kerala.
  • During last decade highest improvement in literacy rate was observed in Rural Females.

Increase in Literacy Rate: 9.2%

Rural and Urban Divide

  • Rural: 833.1 M (68.8%).
  • Top 3 States: Uttar Pradesh > Bihar > West Bengal.
  • Bottom 3 States: Sikkim > Mizoram > Goa.
  • Urban: 377.1 Million (31.2%).
  • Top 3 States: Maharashtra > Uttar Pradesh > Tamil Nadu.
  • Bottom 3 States: Sikkim > Arunachal Pradesh > Mizoram.

Highest % of rural population: Lakshadweep (among UTs).

Highest % of urban population: Delhi.

Chandigarh and Lakshadweep are the most urbanised UT.

Daman & Diu has the highest % of rural population.

Percentage-wise Rural and Urban Divide

  • Rural (highest): Himachal Pradesh (89.9%) > Bihar (88.7) > Assam (85.92%).
  • Urban (highest): Goa (62.17%) > Tamil Nadu (48.4%) > Kerala (47.7%).

Caste-Based Population

Scheduled Caste (SC) Population: 201 Million (16.6% of the total population).

  • Highest population: Uttar Pradesh.
  • Highest percentage-wise population: Punjab.
  • Lowest population: Mizoram.
  • Lowest percentage-wise: Mizoram.
  • State/UTs with 0% SC population: Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep.

Scheduled Tribe (ST) Population: 104.3 Million (8.6% of the total population).

  • Highest population: Madhya Pradesh.
  • Highest percentage-wise population: Lakshadweep.
  • Lowest population: Haryana > Punjab > Delhi > Puducherry > Chandigarh (these three states have zero ST population).

Demographic Dividend

  • A demographic dividend is a period of economic growth that happens when a country's population ages and the working-age population increases.
  • Working age group in India: 15-64 or 15-59.

Work Force in India

  • Male work force participation: 53.26%.
  • Female work force participation: 25.5%.
  • Himachal has the highest female LFPR (Labor Force Participation Rate) in rural India (47.4%).
  • Tamil Nadu has the highest female LFPR in urban India.

Migration Trends

  • Highest out-migration states: Uttar Pradesh > Bihar.
  • Highest in-migration state: Maharashtra.
  • Percentage of total migrants from Nepal: 15.1%.
  • Percentage of total migrants from Sri Lanka: 2.9%.

Main Reason for Migration

  • For men: Work and employment.
  • For women: Marriage.
  • The 1st Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) was first conducted in 1931 by Ministry of Rural Development.
  • According to 2011 Census, 2.21% of India's population (i.e. 26.8 Million) were identified as disabled.
  • Adolescent population: 21% (10-19 yrs).

Miscellaneous Facts

  • Census 2024 will be conducted through Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) which is a Digitalized System.
  • National Population Policy (NPP) 2000: It aims to achieve a stable population by 2045.
